extracted.intended_audience: in-house counsel, corporate secretaries, SEC reporting officers, and compliance professionals responsible for U.S. Form 8-K filings
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, item-by-item guidance summarizing when a Form 8-K is required, the specific disclosures required for each item, and practice tips for timing, drafting, and follow-up. Focused on U.S. SEC reporting obligations under Form 8-K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2.06 — Material Impairments (8-K trigger and required disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8-K is required if the company’s board, a board committee, or an authorized officer concludes that a material charge for impairment to one or more of the company’s assets is required under generally accepted accounting principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required disclosure items: date of conclusion that a material charge is required; description of the impaired assets; facts and circumstances leading to the conclusion; an estimate of the amount or range of amounts of the impairment charge; an estimate of the amount or range of amounts of the impairment charge that will result in future cash expenditures. Key notes and practice tips: (1) If unable to make a good faith estimate of the amount in the initial 8-K, the company must amend the Form 8-K within four business days after it formulates an estimate (company should provide an estimate whenever possible because inability to provide could trigger adverse investor reaction). (2) Implement procedures to distinguish a concluded impairment determination from an impairment merely under active consideration. (3) Consider reporting under Item 2.01 when impaired assets are significant. (4) Terminology and scope are based on ASC 360-10; reportable impairments include securities and goodwill. (5) No 8-K required if the impairment conclusion is made in connection with (or coincides with) preparation/review/audit of financial statements required to be included in the next periodic report, the report is timely filed, and the impairment conclusion is disclosed in that report. (6) SEC CDI cross-references (e.g., Question 110.01 and 110.02) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 3.01 — Notice of Delisting or Failure to Satisfy Continued Listing Rule; Transfer of Listing
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8-K is required when the company receives notice from the principal national securities exchange that the company or a class of its securities does not satisfy a continued listing rule or standard, the exchange has applied to the SEC to delist the securities, the exchange has taken all necessary steps to delist, the company notifies the exchange it is aware of material noncompliance, the exchange issues a public reprimand letter or similar communication, or the company has taken definitive action to withdraw or transfer a listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required disclosure elements include the rule or standard in question and, depending on the sub-item: date of notice or action; any action or response the company has determined to take at time of filing (for notices under 3.01(a)/(b)); date and summary of contents for a public reprimand (3.01(c)); and for listing withdrawal actions (3.01(d)) the definitive action taken. Practice tips: (1) Disclosure is required even if the company has a grace or cure period. (2) In involuntary delisting cases, multiple Form 8-Ks may be required (initial notice and ultimate delisting). (3) Subsequent notices on the same rule/standard generally do not require new 8-Ks. (4) Although not required, companies may amend or file a new 8-K to report return to compliance. (5) Develop early-warning systems (e.g., track minimum bid price even for one day). (6) Item 3.01 does not apply to companies exclusively traded OTC; certain routine/noncontroversial delistings (e.g., redemption of an entire class) may not trigger 3.01(a). (7) Companies need not file the actual exchange notice as an exhibit. (8) Where rules require disclosure of actions/responses determined at filing time, the company should disclaim intent to update the 8-K for later-decided actions, but must evaluate whether new material facts require additional disclosure. (9) Definitive action can include board resolutions to delist. (10) NYSE/Nasdaq-specific governance filing cross-checks (e.g., Nasdaq Rule 5625) may create parallel obligations to consider materiality and 8-K triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 3.02 — Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities (trigger, thresholds, and required disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8-K is required if the company sells equity securities in a transaction not registered under the Securities Act, unless sales in the aggregate since the last report or last periodic report constitute less than 1% of outstanding securities of that class (5% threshold for smaller reporting companies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required disclosure follows paragraphs (a) and (c)-(e) of Item 701 of Regulation S-K and specifically includes: date of sale and title and amount of securities sold; for cash sales, aggregate offering price and aggregate underwriting discounts/commissions; for non-cash sales, nature of the transaction and nature and aggregate amount of consideration received; exemption from Securities Act registration claimed and facts relied upon; terms of conversion/exercise when securities are convertible/exchangeable/warrants/options. Practice tips and notes: (1) 'Equity securities' includes convertible debt and options exercisable for common stock. (2) Grants of options under employee plans may not be 'sales' until exercise; reporting triggers at exercise if not covered by Form S-8 and threshold exceeded. (3) Sales of a class not currently outstanding may exceed the threshold and trigger reporting. (4) Disclosure is not required until the company enters an agreement enforceable against it, or, if no agreement exists, after closing/settlement. (5) Special rules for wholly owned subsidiaries receiving investments from parents. (6) Outstanding share count is determined on an actual outstanding basis, not fully-diluted. (7) Unregistered sales of warrants/options/convertible notes can trigger reporting; disclosing maximum underlying securities can avoid later triggers. (8) Maintain a running count/system for unregistered sales and typical sources (Rule 144A, PIPEs, inducement grants, private-placement M&A). (9) Information omitted from an 8-K may still be reportable in Form 10-Q/10-K if not previously reported; consider whether to include underwriting/identity information in 8-K given safe-harbor concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 3.03 — Material Modifications to Rights of Security Holders
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8-K is required if the constituent instruments (charter, indenture, etc.) defining holders' rights have been materially modified, or the rights of any class of registered securities have been materially limited or qualified by issuance or modification of another class of securities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required disclosures: date of modification or issuance; title of class of securities involved; brief description of general effect of modification or issuance. Practice tips: working capital restrictions and other dividend payment limitations are examples that must be reported. Triggers related to shareholder rights plans occur upon issuance of a dividend of preferred share purchase right (though entering into a shareholder rights plan that is a material definitive agreement may trigger Item 1.01 and filing of a certificate of designation may trigger Item 5.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 4.01 — Changes in Registrant’s Certifying Accountant (departure and engagement disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8-K is required when an independent accountant previously engaged as the principal accountant resigns, declines to stand for re-appointment, or is dismissed, or when a new independent accountant is engaged as the principal accountant or an accountant on whom the principal accountant is expected to express reliance regarding a significant subsidiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required disclosure for departure: state whether the former accountant 'resigned,' 'declined to stand for re-election' or was 'dismissed' (use one of those three specific terms) and the date; provide other information required by Item 304(a)(1) of Regulation S-K including whether the former accountant's audit reports for either of the past two years contained an adverse opinion, disclaimer, or qualification; whether the decision to change accountants was recommended/approved by the audit committee (or board if no audit committee); and whether there have been disagreements or reportable events during the two most recent fiscal years and any interim period through termination (with details). Comply with Item 304(a)(3) requirements: provide the former accountant with a copy of disclosures, request a letter indicating whether it agrees with the disclosures, and file that letter as an exhibit. For engagement: identify the newly engaged accountant and date of engagement and provide information required by Item 304(a)(2) regarding prior consultations. Practice tips/key rules: (1) If termination and engagement do not coincide, two separate 8-Ks may be required. (2) Engaging a new accountant for next fiscal year while predecessor completes the current audit may be deemed a termination and must be reported. (3) Amendments to Item 4.01 require filing an updated auditor letter. (4) If a predecessor refuses to furnish an agreement letter, indicate that fact in the 8-K or by amendment. (5) Form 8-K must be used even when the event occurs within four business days before filing a Form 10-Q/10-K. (6) Use only the three specified S-K Item 304 terms — other wording will likely prompt SEC comment. (7) If an accountant resigns/dismissed due to PCAOB registration revocation, disclose that fact. (8) Changes among related/affiliate accounting firms (separate legal entities registered with PCAOB) still require Item 4.01. (9) Evaluate business combinations of accounting firms for reporting obligations. (10) Timing: file Item 4.01 within four business days of the change in accountants (or within four business days of decision when applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 4.02 — Non-Reliance on Previously Issued Financial Statements or Related Audit Report
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8-K is required if the company (board, committee, or authorized officers) concludes that any previously issued financial statements should no longer be relied upon because of an error (ASC 250), or if the company is advised by or receives notice from its independent accountant that disclosure should be made or action taken to prevent future reliance on an audit report or completed interim review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required disclosure: date of conclusion or accountant notification; identification of affected financial statements; brief description of the facts underlying the conclusion (to the extent known) or information provided by the accountant; statement whether the audit committee (or board if no audit committee) or authorized officers discussed the subject matter with the independent accountant; provision of the written notice received from the accountant as Exhibit 7 for an accountant determination. Additional procedural requirements for an Accountant Determination: provide the independent accountant with a copy of the company's disclosure no later than the same day it files with the SEC; request the accountant furnish promptly a letter to the SEC stating whether it agrees with the company's statements and, if not, stating disagreements; amend the previously filed Form 8-K to file the accountant's letter as an exhibit within two business days of receipt. Practice tips: (1) Provide any proposed disclosure to the accountant in advance to obtain input when possible. (2) Use Form 8-K to report events even if they occur within four business days before filing a Form 10-Q or 10-K. (3) If the company already filed under Item 4.02(a), it generally does not need a second Form 8-K under Item 4.02(b) for the same error unless the auditor's conclusion concerns a different error. (4) Item 4.02 does not apply to pro forma financial information (amend the form containing pro forma information if errors are found). (5) Errors in interactive data files that do not affect financial statements do not trigger Item 4.02; amend the original form to correct interactive data. (6) After filing an Item 4.02, evaluate whether the company can continue to sell securities under existing registration statements; consult counsel. (7) Review Section 4600 of the SEC Division of Corporation Finance's FRM and CDIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.01 — Changes in Control of Registrant (trigger and required disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8-K is required when, to the knowledge of the board, a board committee, or authorized officers, a change in control has occurred, or there is an arrangement known to the company that may result in a change in control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required disclosure where a change in control has occurred: identity of person who acquired control; identity of person from whom control was assumed; date and description of the transaction resulting in the change; basis of control (including percentage of voting securities owned by acquiring person after change); amount of consideration used by acquiring person; source of funds used by acquiring person (subject to certain exceptions, e.g., certain bank loans in ordinary course); any arrangements or understandings among members of both former and new control groups regarding director elections or other matters. Where there is an arrangement that may result in a change, describe the arrangements known as required by Item 403(c) of Regulation S-K, including any pledge of securities. Practice tips: (1) Disclosure of the source of acquiring person’s funds is subject to exceptions (certain bank loans). (2) In describing arrangements under Item 403(c), companies need not describe ordinary default provisions contained in charters/indentures/governing instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.02 — Departures, Elections, Appointments, and Compensatory Arrangements for Directors and Certain Officers
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8-K is required for multiple events: (a) a director's resignation/refusal to stand for re-election due to a disagreement with the company (or removal for cause); (b) departure of principal officers or named executive officers or directors for reasons not covered by (a); (c) appointment of a principal officer; (d) election of a director (outside security-holder vote); (e) material compensatory plans/agreements/awards for principal officers or named executive officers; and (f) later executive compensation determinations that make previously omitted salary/bonus amounts calculable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required disclosures vary by sub-item: For 5.02(a) (departure due to disagreement): date of resignation/refusal/removal; positions held on any board committee; brief description of circumstances representing the disagreement (company must file any written correspondence provided by the director as an exhibit regardless of director request); provide the director a copy of the disclosures the same day and an opportunity to furnish a letter stating agreement/disagreement, and file any such letter as an exhibit within two business days of receipt. For 5.02(b) (other departures): state that event occurred; date of event; effective date. For 5.02(c) (appointment): officer’s name and position; date of appointment; biographical information as required by Item 401(b) and family relationships per Item 401(d); business experience per Item 401(e); related person transactions per Item 404(a); brief description of any material plan/contract/arrangement entered into or materially amended in connection with appointment and any related grants/awards (or state info unavailable and amend within four business days when determined). For 5.02(d) (election): new director’s name; date of election; brief description of any arrangement/understanding under which selected; board committee assignments (or statement if unavailable and amend within four business days); related person transaction info per Item 404(a) (or amend within four business days); brief description of material plans/contracts/awards entered into or amended in connection with election. For 5.02(e) (compensatory arrangements): brief description of terms and amounts payable. For 5.02(f) (later determinations): name of named executive officer; the omitted salary and bonus amounts; a recalculated total compensation figure reflecting the new info; if the officer is the principal executive officer and pay-ratio disclosure is required, include the pay-ratio disclosure. Practice tips and definitions: 'Principal officer' defined (PEO, president, PFO, principal accounting officer, principal operating officer or similar); 'named executive officer' defined by prior proxy/Form 10-K disclosure; if certain required information is not determined at time of filing, include a statement and amend within four business days after the information is determined or becomes available. Additional practice tips cross-reference other Items (e.g., filing under Item 1.01 or Item 5.03 where applicable).
